summary.text: A 42-year-old Caucasian male office worker with a history of orthotopic heart transplantation in late 1999 for end-stage dilated cardiomyopathy was first examined at a dental center in early 2002 because of an inadequate prosthetic crown on the upper right central incisor. He was maintained on lifelong immunosuppressive therapy with cyclosporine, mycophenolate mofetil and bisoprolol, without calcium channel blockers, and denied tobacco, alcohol and recreational drug use.

At the 2002 examination he had generalized lobulated, erythematous gingival overgrowth with hypertrophic interdental papillae, probing depths of 4-5 mm at multiple localized sites, bleeding on probing, plaque accumulation and 1-2 mm attachment loss in some areas. The condition was consistent with drug-induced gingival overgrowth, most likely related to cyclosporine, with gingivitis and localized Stage I, Grade A periodontitis. Phase I periodontal therapy and replacement of the prosthetic crown were provided.

He remained under maintenance care for more than two decades with periodontal stability confirmed by charting and radiographs, but compliance declined and maintenance care was discontinued for approximately three years.

In 2025 he returned with significant periodontal deterioration consistent with localized Stage II, Grade B periodontitis, flaring of the maxillary central incisors, purulent exudate, tooth discoloration and bleeding on probing, with concern about aesthetics and function rather than pain. He had a single session of full-mouth scaling and root planing under local anesthesia, declined gingivectomy and gingivoplasty, and was scheduled for supportive periodontal therapy every three months.

DNA-based metagenomic sequencing of subgingival plaque and tongue dorsum showed a dysbiotic subgingival profile and a relatively eubiotic tongue profile, and no Candida spp. were detected. After the 2025 re-intervention bleeding on probing, gingival inflammation and oral hygiene improved, probing depths remained stable in the most affected areas, adherence improved after discussion of the metagenomic results, and the gingival overgrowth was not fully resolved, with the cyclosporine regimen unmodifiable and surgery declined.

caption_evidence.quote:
Figure 9
Relative abundance of bacterial taxa identified in the subgingival plaque sample from the maxillary central incisors pocket, collected during the 2025 follow-up visit, revealing a dysbiotic microbial profile. The red-colored slice represents the relative abundance of Porphyromonas gingivalis, a keystone pathogen implicated in the onset and progression of periodontal disease. Of particular note, the detection of Fusobacterium nucleatum highlights its ecological role as a bridging organism contributing to subgingival biofilm maturation and dysbiosis.Figure created by the authors using open-source software (Python/matplotlib).
